grave_salaam_buraidah.title: Greeting at the Graveyard (Narration of Buraidah)
grave_salaam_buraidah.arabicText: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ لَاحِقُونَ، أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ لَنَا وَلَكُمُ الْعَافِيَةَ
grave_salaam_buraidah.transliteration: As-salamu 'alaykum ahlad-diyari minal-mu'minina wal-muslimeen, wa inna insha'Allahu bikum lahiqun. As'alullaha lana wa lakumul-'afiyah.
grave_salaam_buraidah.translation: Peace be upon you, O inhabitants of the dwellings, believers and Muslims. And indeed we, if Allah wills, will join you. I ask Allah for well-being for us and for you.
grave_salaam_buraidah.benefit: This is the comprehensive greeting the Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach his companions when they visited the graveyard. It greets the deceased, acknowledges our own mortality, and asks Allah for well-being for both the living and the dead. A profound reminder of the Day we will all meet.

grave_salaam_aisha.title: Greeting Taught to Aisha
grave_salaam_aisha.arabicText: السَّلَامُ عَلَىٰ أَهْلِ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمِينَ، وَيَرْحَمُ اللَّهُ الْمُسْتَقْدِمِينَ مِنَّا وَالْمُسْتَأْخِرِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ لَاحِقُونَ
grave_salaam_aisha.transliteration: As-salamu 'ala ahlid-diyari minal-mu'minina wal-muslimeen, wa yarhamullahul-mustaqdimina minna wal-musta'khireen, wa inna insha'Allahu bikum lahiqun.
grave_salaam_aisha.translation: Peace be upon the inhabitants of the abodes, believers and Muslims. May Allah have mercy upon those who have gone ahead of us and those who come later on, and indeed we shall, if Allah wills, join you.
grave_salaam_aisha.benefit: Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) asked the Prophet (ﷺ) what she should say when visiting the graves, and he instructed her to recite these words. This narration contains a beautiful prayer — asking Allah's mercy upon all generations, from the earliest who passed away to those yet to come. A profound dua that spans all of humanity.
